questions.question: How does changing the number of turns of wire in an electromagnet's coil affect its magnetic field strength?
options: Increasing the number of turns increases the magnetic field strength.
Increasing the number of turns decreases the magnetic field strength.
Changing the number of turns has no effect on the magnetic field strength.
Increasing the number of turns only works if the wire is non-metal.

questions.question: Which of the following changes will make the magnetic field of an electromagnet stronger?
options: Reducing the voltage of the power source.
Increasing the electric current flowing through the coil.
Using a wire with higher electrical resistance to lower the current.
Keeping the current extremely low.

questions.question: Why is an electromagnet constructed with bare, uninsulated wire unable to function if the adjacent turns touch each other?
options: The current short-circuits across the touching turns instead of flowing through the coil.
The metal turns will melt instantly due to high friction.
The bare wire prevents any magnetic fields from forming around individual wire segments.
The electricity is blocked from entering the core entirely.

questions.question: What is the primary reason why adding a soft iron core to an electromagnet increases its overall strength?
options: The soft iron core conducts heat away from the coil.
The soft iron core becomes magnetised when the electromagnet is turned on.
The core permanently retains its magnetism even when the current is switched off.
The soft iron core acts as an insulator to prevent short-circuits.

questions.question: What occurs immediately around a straight wire when an electric current begins to flow through it?
options: A static electric charge builds up on the outer surface.
A magnetic field is generated around the wire.
The wire begins to spin on its axis.
The surrounding air becomes permanently magnetised.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of an electromagnet compared to a permanent magnet?
options: It can be switched on and off using an electric current.
It does not require any materials to be magnetic.
It has only a north pole and no south pole.
It retains its magnetic field forever without needing a power source.

questions.question: If you bring the north-seeking pole of one bar magnet close to the north-seeking pole of another, what will happen?
options: They will attract each other.
They will repel each other.
They will cancel each other out and lose their magnetism.
They will rotate to point towards the South Pole.

questions.question: How do magnetic materials behave when they are placed near the poles of a bar magnet?
options: They are attracted to the north-seeking pole but repelled by the south-seeking pole.
They are repelled by both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles.
They are attracted to both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles.
They are only attracted to the south-seeking pole.

questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only the three metal elements that are magnetic?
options: Iron, copper, and aluminium
Gold, silver, and platinum
Iron, cobalt, and nickel
Lead, tin, and zinc

questions.question: Why does the north-seeking pole of a suspended bar magnet point towards the Earth's geographic North Pole?
options: The Earth is surrounded by a vacuum that pulls on magnets.
The Earth has its own magnetic field.
Gravity pulls the heavier north-seeking pole downwards.
The North Pole contains large deposits of pure copper.

questions.question: How does a plotting compass behave when placed near a bar magnet?
options: Its needle spins continuously in circles.
Its needle lines up with the magnetic field of the magnet.
Its needle points directly to the nearest electric socket.
Its needle is repelled and points perpendicular to the field lines.

questions.question: If you trace a magnetic field line outside a magnet, where does it start and end?
options: From the north-seeking pole to the south-seeking pole.
From the south-seeking pole to the north-seeking pole.
From the centre of the magnet outwards in straight lines.
From the electrical terminal to the iron core.

questions.question: What do the arrows drawn on magnetic field lines represent?
options: The path that electrons take when flowing through the magnet.
The direction of the electric current in the nearest wire.
The direction in which the north-seeking pole of another magnet would be forced.
The speed at which the magnetic field is expanding.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true property of magnetic field lines?
options: They cross over each other where the magnetic field is weakest.
They are continuous and do not cross over.
They start and end at the exact same pole.
They form sharp, jagged angles around the corners of a magnet.

questions.question: In an electric bell, what is the role of the electromagnet?
options: It heats up a metal strip to break the circuit.
It attracts and moves the striker so that it hits the bell.
It generates electricity to power the striker's spring.
It permanently magnetises the gong to keep it ringing.

questions.question: How does an electric bell allow its striker to spring back after hitting the bell?
options: The electromagnet reverses its magnetic poles.
The user must manually release a switch.
The movement of the striker breaks its own circuit, turning off the electromagnet.
The battery runs out of charge instantly.

questions.question: What causes the spinning coil of wire inside an electric motor to rotate?
options: The heat generated by the electric current pushes it around.
Other magnets around the spinning coil push it round when there is a current.
The wire coil unravels and winds up repeatedly.
Gravity pulls the heavier side of the coil downwards.
